paragraphs: Friend, here's the heavy truth of this chapter. Solomon's throne wasn't built on his own cleverness. He says it himself: the LORD is "the One who established me, who set me on the throne of my father David, and who founded for me a dynasty as He promised" (1 Kings 2:24). The chapter closes with "Thus the kingdom was firmly established in the hand of Solomon" (1 Kings 2:46), and a promise God made is what holds it up.

Now look at the three men who ran into Solomon's king-sized judgment. Adonijah said the kingship "has come to him from the LORD" (1 Kings 2:15), and then asked for something that cost him his life. Joab ran to the altar, and Shimei said "The sentence is fair" (1 Kings 2:38) and then crossed the line he'd sworn not to cross. I think the lesson is that saying the right words isn't the same as living them out. I get nervous just thinking about it, because I've said "I'll be right there" to a hot oven timer and meant it less than I should have.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery today, baker. God keeps His promises, and what He establishes, nobody can shake. Our job is to honor what we say before Him, because words and oaths are not decoration. And this story isn't over, because Solomon's kingdom is only just getting started, so keep your apron on.
